payloads.release_notes:
# OnionHEN v0.9.0

OnionHEN is a homebrew enabler and Toolbox for jailbroken PS5 consoles, built on etaHEN. It prepares the system, injects a Toolbox into the home screen, and adds cheats, a game overlay, payload management, and background services.

**Version:** v0.9.0 is the stable release following v0.9.0-beta1 and v0.9.0-beta2. It brings together their changes since [v0.0.13](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN/releases/tag/v0.0.13).

**Firmware:** Adds support for **13.0-13.6** and **some 5.50 consoles**, alongside the firmware supported by v0.0.13. Please include your exact firmware and console behavior when reporting a problem.

**Download:** `OnionHEN.elf` (Release build; SHA-256: `1f1f7c883d5d998be1d95d7d80b718f85180f8156f257661b0f445a7c6b7c212`).

## What changed since v0.0.13

### Firmware compatibility

This release adds support for firmware **13.0-13.6** and **some 5.50 consoles**. Reports from real hardware are welcome.

### Cheats

On firmware 4.03, opening the cheats menu for a game with no cheats could take about 40 seconds, then leave the home screen unresponsive until a forced reboot ([#97](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN/issues/97), [#103](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN/issues/103)). The beta2 fix makes an empty menu return in a few seconds without stalling ShellUI. The reporter on #103 confirmed the problem was gone in an early beta2 build.

Long cheat names are also truncated on UTF-8 boundaries.

### elfldr

v0.0.13 needed elfldr v0.22 because it loaded the cache through a `file:` URI. v0.9.0 sends a normal ELF to port **9021**, so older elfldr builds work again. An external elfldr must still be listening on 9021.

### Also

- The bundled kstuff is **kstuff-lite 1.11**, up from 1.10 in v0.0.13.
- Toolbox strings cover the remaining PS5 system languages. Startup toasts credit the author and thank contributors; the thanks toast can be turned off in Preferences. The About page lists testers and donors.

payloads.author: saawant12
payloads.release_notes:
**Archive.org sign-in comes to Orbit.**

- **Archive.org sign-in.** Connect your account in the native PS5 app, browser or Orbit Zero to access downloads that require signing in.
- **225 unavailable Archive.org links removed, and 3 games also had to go.** Links that require an Archive.org account are still included.

## Orbit Store · Native PS5 app (FFPKG) and browser (ELF)

- **Smoother Vikingfile and AkiraBox downloads.** Complete the provider’s verification, then wait. Orbit automatically captures the download link and returns you to the app, without manually pressing Download.

## Orbit Zero · Mac, Windows and Linux

- **TorBox downloads on your computer.** Connect TorBox in Download settings, download through supported sources and transfer to your PS5.
- **Recover completed downloads from your computer cache.** Restore a removed download entry and transfer the saved file without downloading it again.
- **Reconnect after your PS5's address changes.** Update its address and verify the connection. Recovery is also available after pairing has been reset.
- **Better download and transfer recovery.** Interrupted computer downloads retry automatically. Resume stalled PS5 transfers or remove stuck entries from Downloads while keeping their files.
- **Clearer errors.** See which stage needs attention and open the original source page directly.

[Install Orbit Zero on Mac, Windows or Linux](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/blob/main/guides/orbit-zero-installation.md) · [Set up a PS5 without internet](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/blob/main/guides/orbit-zero-offline-ps5.md) · [Update Orbit Store on PS5](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/blob/main/guides/getting-started.md#update-the-tv-app)

payloads.name: ShadowMountPlus-beta
payloads.description: A fully automated, background 'Auto-Mounter' payload for Jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles. (Beta/pre-release channel.)
payloads.author: drakmor
payloads.release_notes:
- **Removed legacy kstuff auto-pause and delay autotuning.** Use the latest version of kstuff and do not use EtaHEN.
- Added per-game and default fakelib modes: Full, Emulators only, and Disabled, configurable through the web UI.
- Prevented libkernel.sprx from entering fakelib overlays, using filtered caches for images and installed PKGs.
- Fixed backport mounting when cleanup files or the fakelib directory are missing; missing files are silently skipped.
- Added read-only access to system fonts `/preinst/common/font` inside game sandboxes.
- Fixed sandbox storage mounts on USB connection/disconnection and disc insertion/ejection. Only mounted `/mnt/usb*`, `/mnt/ext*`, and `/mnt/disc` volumes are exposed.
- Improved game error reporting during the first 60 seconds after launch, including fatal-signal details and crash addresses when available.
- Added automatic ShellCore hook recovery after resume and before game registration.
- Added game versions to compact and full web cards; fixed icons for games on extended storage.
- Improved missing-source handling, localized operation errors, and updated web UI translations.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus/compare/1.7beta4...1.7beta5

payloads.name: pegasus-dl
payloads.author: pegasus-ps5
payloads.release_notes:
- Parallel downloads now use persistent connections and write ranges directly
  into the temporary file, avoiding a final segment-copy pass. New configurations
  default to 16 connections, with a single-stream fallback for incompatible hosts.
- RAR/RAR5 and 7z archive cache downloads use the same parallel engine. Paused
  downloads resume from checked checkpoints, and paused extraction restarts from
  the completed cache without downloading again.
- Completed RAR caches survive password prompts and wrong passwords. UTF-8
  passwords and retries for legacy encrypted RAR files are handled correctly.
- Extraction progress now counts bytes across files. Cancellation and
  finalization are coordinated to avoid committing cancelled work.
- Archive replacement failures restore the previous destination, stored RAR
  entries receive CRC checks, and failed format probes clean up their temporary
  files.

payloads.name: elf-arsenal
payloads.author: soniciso
payloads.release_notes:
Firmware coverage, a PKG installer that takes links, and a download queue that
stops hiding what it is doing.

## PKG Installer

**Install from a link.** Paste URLs one per line, or give it the address of a
page that lists them — an archive.org item, an open directory index, anything
that is just anchors — and the console reads that page and hands back the .pkg
links to pick from. Doing the fetch on the console also sidesteps the CORS
refusals a browser would hit. Links go on a queue with a single worker, since
installs serialise down there anyway; it reports per-item state and refuses
duplicates that are still pending.

## Firmware coverage

Every payload is rebuilt against the current SDK, so all of them now carry the
full 3.00–13.60 dispatch. zftpd was the one that mattered: it stopped at 10.60
and was reachable from the FTP daemon switch. The firmware check that catches
this now also runs on the argv spawn path, which was skipping it.

The ShellCore PPR patch gains tables for **6.50** and **10.60**, taking it to 50
of 51 firmwares — only 9.05 is missing, and no image for it exists to derive one
from. Both new tables were carried over from neighbouring firmwares rather than
read off a console; `tools/verify-firmware-tables.py` checks every table against
a real firmware image and all 51 pass, 561 sites, nothing failing. The same tool
verifies kmonitor's kernel offsets against decrypted kernels — 51 of 52.

**The patcher now looks before it writes.** Each entry replaces a specific
instruction, and nothing checked that the instruction was there; an offset that
did not describe the running build was written anyway. Anything unexpected is
skipped now, which is also what makes a derived table safe to ship.

payloads.name: ps5debug-NG
payloads.description: PS5 debugger payload - userland TCP wire-protocol server hosted inside SceShellCore.
payloads.author: OpenSourcereR-dev
payloads.release_notes:
# ps5debug-NG v1.3.2

v1.3.0 was the big feature release. **v1.3.2 is the correctness and reliability release** that follows it: writes now prove they landed, three separate session-killing bugs are fixed, a scan comparator that silently returned wrong results is repaired, and firmware support extends through **FW 13.60**.

There was no separate v1.3.1 download, so **this release also contains everything from v1.3.1** (Turbo Scan cancel).

---

### ⚠️ Read this first: writes are now verified, and that changes what you see

Process writes used to report success as soon as the write was handed off. They are now **read back and compared before success is reported**, so a write that silently did nothing now correctly reports a failure.

**If you are a client developer:** a write that previously appeared to succeed may now return `CMD_ERROR`. That is the bug surfacing, not a new bug. Servers advertise **capability level `1.1`** so clients can detect the behaviour.

- `CMD_PROC_WRITE` returns terminal `CMD_ERROR` on write or verification failure.
- Write-multi returns **typed per-entry status codes** (invalid / DMAP / verify / mdbg) so you can tell exactly which entries failed and why, instead of losing the detail in one aggregate result.
- A proven DMAP mismatch no longer quietly falls through to the mdbg path.
- **Caveat:** a transfer whose start address ends in `0xFF` backs up one byte to keep the write aligned. That adjacent-byte read-modify-write is not atomic, so it needs a **stable or suspended target** to be safe.

---

### 🛠️ Session-killing bugs fixed

- **Fixed a debug session wedge that required a console reboot.** Toggling a trainer patch while the target was stopped at a breakpoint could deadlock the sole debug worker: an RPC stop was issued against a process the debugger already held ptrace-stopped, so the wait never returned, the worker died, and every reattach afterwards failed (clients reported "Process not connected" / already-debugging) until the console was restarted.

payloads.author: juma-sayeh
payloads.release_notes:
# Game Compressor 1.0.4

Game Compressor 1.0.4 adds a multilingual interface and improves compatibility
with firmware 4.51, APR-EMU folder workflows, and ShadowMountPlus launch
layouts.

Compared against `v1.0.3`.

## Key Changes

- Added German, French, Arabic, Italian, Spanish, and Simplified Chinese
  translations, with automatic system-language selection and a saved manual
  language selector.
- Added right-to-left layout support for Arabic and localized Game Compressor
  launcher titles for every supported language.
- Improved firmware 4.51 browser compatibility and added clearer web-server
  startup diagnostics.
- Improved relaunch handling when a previous Game Compressor instance leaves
  port 5910 open but no longer answers the local HTTP handoff.
- Added ShadowMountPlus executable discovery under `/data/ps5_autoloader` in
  addition to Payload Manager locations.

## Fixes

- Fixed `Build AMPR Index` for directly detected game folders so enqueue and
  worker resolution use the same APR-EMU probe result.
- Fixed APR-EMU module file permissions for affected deployment and loading
  paths.
- Fixed the compression wizard so `Delete after verified` keeps its own
  free-space and deletion explanation when switching source-preservation
  options.

See `CHANGELOG.md` for the full detailed change list.
